subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (1, −2, 1), (0, 1, −1) and (3, −1, 1), then show that A³ − 3A² − A − 3I = O.

mark_split.label: Combine the four terms and show the result is O

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.54 — SAQ chapter 7 Matrices, answer 43.2, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: TS 19. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer (the only SAQ in the chapter that carries them is answer 40 on book p.51, printed 1+1+1+1). The 1+2+1 above puts half the marks on A³, because A³ can only be reached AFTER A² and so carries the compounding risk: an error in A² is invisible until A³ fails to cancel. The book's SAQ chapter header carries ★★★ and reads "4 Marks"; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q11 is the Matrices slot.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — say what you have to work out first, what comes next, and what happens at the end.

steps.label: Find A²
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiply row by column. Watch the negative entries — row 1 against column 2 is 1(−2) + (−2)(1) + 1(−1) = −5, and a dropped minus here carries through into A³ as well.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply row by column, watching the negatives: row 1 against column 2 is 1(−2) + (−2)(1) + 1(−1) = −5.

recall.must_convey: That A² is A multiplied by itself row against column — not each entry squared.
accept: A squared is A times A using row into column multiplication
multiply the matrix by itself to get A squared
find A into A carefully because of the negative entries
A square ante A into A, row into column multiply cheyyali
do the matrix multiplication of A with itself

steps.why: A³ is built from A², so this matrix is used twice. It is worth checking one entry against the original before going on, because nothing later will point back to an error made here.
common_mistakes: Squaring each entry instead of multiplying the matrices.
Dropping a minus sign in a product of two negative entries.

steps.label: Find A³
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. A³ = A²·A — use the matrix just found, not A three times over. Nine more row-by-column products, and the numbers are larger now.
steps.memory_tip: A³ = A²·A — use the matrix just found, not A three times over.

recall.must_convey: That A³ is found as A² multiplied by A, reusing the matrix already computed.
accept: A cubed is A squared times A so multiply the matrix already found by A
use A squared and multiply it by A again to get A cubed
A three is A two into A, row into column
A cube ante A square ni A tho multiply cheyyali
multiply the previous result by A once more

steps.why: Matrix multiplication is associative, so A·A·A can be grouped as (A·A)·A. Reusing A² halves the work and is why the order of the steps matters.
common_mistakes: Multiplying A by A by A from scratch and making a fresh arithmetic error.
Multiplying A² by A² and calling the result A³ — that gives A⁴; A³ is A²·A.
Sign slips in the larger numbers.

steps.label: Combine the four terms
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Write out 3A², A and 3I, then subtract entry by entry. Every one of the nine entries must come to zero — check a few in full rather than assuming the pattern.
steps.memory_tip: Write out 3A², A and 3I, then subtract entry by entry. All nine entries must come to zero.
lines: Every entry cancels in the same way:

recall.must_convey: That 3A², A and 3I are subtracted from A³ entry by entry, and that every entry comes out zero, giving the zero matrix O.
accept: subtract three A squared and A and three I from A cubed entry by entry and every entry is zero
combine all four matrices and each of the nine entries cancels to give the null matrix
take A cubed minus three A squared minus A minus three I and it comes to O
nalugu matrices ni entry by entry subtract cheste anni zero avthai
the four terms cancel completely giving the zero matrix

steps.why: O is the ZERO matrix, not the number 0. And because every entry has to cancel independently, this step is also the check on all the arithmetic before it — if one entry survives, A² or A³ is wrong.
common_mistakes: Writing "= 0" instead of "= O" — the answer is a matrix.
Forgetting that 3I contributes only on the diagonal.
Checking one entry, finding zero, and asserting the rest.

insider_note: A³ is needed, so A² has to be right before anything else — one slip there ruins both later matrices. Work entry by entry across all four terms; every one of the nine must come to 0.
